heard: A structure three billion light years long should not exist. In 2021, student Alexia Lopez was mapping distant light in the constellation Boaodes. She used the light from ultra-bright quasars like giant flashlights to map out hidden matter in deep space. Using the Sloan Digital Sky Survey, Lopez found a colossal crescent of galaxies stretching 3.3 billion light years across. This giant arc is so massive, it spans 1 15th the radius of the entire observable universe. Standard cosmology says gravity cannot form structures larger than 1.2 billion light years. There simply hasn't been enough time since the Big Bang for something this big to clump together. This gargantuan structure suggests that our basic understanding of the universe is actually broken.
